en.title: Most Frequent Digital Root, Preferring the Larger Digit
en.description:
Repeatedly replace each integer with the sum of its digits until every number is a single digit. Return the digit that appears most often; if counts are tied, take the larger digit.

This site's standard input/output is stated explicitly; ranges not given by the source problem are marked as this site's conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n non-negative integers; 1≤n≤100, 0≤a[i]≤1000000.
en.explanation: Example 1: the digital roots are 6, 6, 6, 2, so return 6. Example 2: 1 and 2 appear once each; on the tie, take 2. Example 3: the digital roots are 0, 9, 9, so return 9; a positive multiple of 9 does not have digital root 0.
hints: The digital root of a positive integer is 1+(x−1)%9, and 0 maps to 0 separately. Count the frequencies of the ten possible results, then compare counts and digits.
